content: It outlines how metronidazole can alter the metabolism of these drugs, primarily through its effects on hepatic and intestinal enzymes such as CYP2C9/10, CYP3A4, and others. These interactions can lead to increased or decreased drug levels, potentially affecting their efficacy or toxicity. Below is a professional interpretation of the content: 1. Metronidazole and Flurbiprofen: Metronidazole may increase the levels or effects of flurbiprofen by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 2. Metronidazole and Fluvastatin: Metronidazole can elevate fluvastatin levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical impact is uncertain. 3. Metronidazole and Ibuprofen (oral and IV): Metronidazole may increase ibuprofen levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 4. Metronidazole and Imatinib: Metronidazole may increase imatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unclear. 5. Metronidazole and Imipramine: Metronidazole can elevate imipramine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance is uncertain. 6. Metronidazole and Irinotecan (including liposomal): Metronidazole may increase irinotecan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. The clinical impact is unknown. 7. Metronidazole and Isradipine: Metronidazole may increase isradipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance is unclear. 8. Metronidazole and Itraconazole: Metronidazole can elevate itraconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. The clinical relevance is uncertain. 9. Metronidazole and Ketoconazole/Levoketoconazole: Metronidazole may increase the levels of these drugs by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance is unknown. 10. Metronidazole and Lithium: Metronidazole increases lithium levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical impact is unclear. 11. Metronidazole and Meloxicam: Metronidazole may increase meloxicam levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10. The significance is uncertain. 12. Metronidazole and Montelukast: Metronidazole can elevate montelukast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unclear. 13. Metronidazole and Nifedipine/Nimodipine/Nitrendipine: Metronidazole may increase the levels of these drugs by inhibiting CYP3A4. The significance is unknown. 14. Metronidazole and Nitroglycerin (IV): Metronidazole may reduce nitroglycerin metabolism, but the clinical impact is unclear. A disulfiram-like reaction is possible. 15. Metronidazole and Oxybutynin: Metronidazole may increase oxybutynin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance is uncertain. 16. Metronidazole and Paclitaxel (including protein-bound): Metronidazole can elevate paclitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. The clinical relevance is unclear. 17. Metronidazole and Pantothenic Acid: Metronidazole may decrease pantothenic acid levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. 18. Metronidazole and Parecoxib: Metronidazole may increase parecoxib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance is unknown. 19. Metronidazole and Pimozide: Metronidazole can elevate pimozide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. The clinical impact is unclear. 20. Metronidazole and Pioglitazone: Metronidazole may increase pioglitazone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance is uncertain. 21. Metronidazole and Piroxicam: Metronidazole can elevate piroxicam levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10. The clinical relevance is unclear. 22. Metronidazole and Propafenone: Metronidazole may increase propafenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance is unknown. 23. Metronidazole and Pyridoxine (oral): Metronidazole may decrease pyridoxine levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. 24. Metronidazole and Quinine: Metronidazole can elevate quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical impact is unclear. 25. Metronidazole and Ramelteon: Metronidazole may increase ramelteon levels by inhibiting both CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4. The significance is uncertain. 26. Metronidazole and Saxagliptin: Metronidazole can elevate saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance is unclear. 27. Metronidazole and Sulfamethoxazole: Metronidazole can elevate sulfamethoxazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10. The clinical impact is unclear. 29. Metronidazole and Thiamine (oral): Metronidazole may decrease thiamine levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. 30. Metronidazole and Avanafil: Metronidazole can elevate avanafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The maximum recommended dose of avanafil should not exceed 50 mg every 24 hours. 46. Metronidazole and Avapritinib: Metronidazole may increase avapritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Metronidazole and BCG Vaccine (live): Metronidazole reduces the effects of the BCG vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism.
